en:
He's an astronaut trainee that trains
hard and can speak multiple languages.
He has good communication skills, is
well-learned, and has a great personality.
He doesn't really act like an Ultimate...

He told me a story about finding a
mysterious map and heading out to
sea to defeat pirates. It went on and on.
I have no idea where he is going with this.

He told me about his summer break, when
he explored a jungle and discovered hidden
ruins. It has nothing to do with being an
astronaut, but it was a cool story.

He says he's trained a lot of "sidekicks"
in the past, but I'm skeptical.
Although, to be fair, his words do
carry a lot of conviction, despite
being a little strange.

He knows my past, but he still believes in
me. He wants to help me move on. I am so
grateful for that support. Kaito, I know it
seems as though you're dragging me
along, but I'll be right there beside you.

He's lost his passion for tennis.
I asked him about his old teammates,
and he seems more than happy to
talk about them, but he says that
that has nothing to do with him anymore.

I asked him about games he played against
his rivals, and it was truly incredible. I never
would have thought that tennis could involve so
many special techniques. But he seemed distant,
and said he didn't want to remember that stuff.

He's thrown away his past—tennis and
a lover he had a future with. He told me
not to care about him, or I'd end up hurt.

Ryoma refused to take a dive in an
underground tennis match fixed by the
mafia. They killed his family for it, 
and Ryoma stained his hands with blood
to get his revenge.

He keeps trying to push me away, saying
I shouldn't care about him, but I can't
help it. I care about my classmates.
Finally, I got him to open up to me a little.

He's the child of wealthy parents and he
travels the world, but those seem unrelated
to his talent. He did mention being a
bad older brother, but I am not sure
what that means...

I asked him about his journeys, and he said
he's seen a lot of evil and corruption in
politics around the world. When pressed, he
smiled and didn't go into detail. I could tell
that he was trying to keep his distance.

No matter what he does, no matter how
hard he tries, he can't quite reach it. I'm
worried about him, now that he's growing
impatient. I try to help him, but he says that
as an only child, I would never understand.

He's searching so hard for his little sister,
and no matter how many times he's told
it's hopeless, he'll never give up. He knows
she's still alive somewhere. I told him that
he should be the "Ultimate Big Brother."

As the Ultimate Detective, I took on his
request to find his missing sisters. I feel
closer to him than ever, now that I've seen
his true smile.

Gonta is obsessed with being a
"gentleman." It's a bit strange that he
grew up in the wild, but his enthusiasm
and his positive attitude is endearing.

The family that raised him for 10 years
is actually lizard people. He has also
fought many martial artists that made
their way through his forest. He must like me
a lot to be comfortable telling me that story.

Gonta wants to be kind, earnest, classy,
polite. A true gentleman. Of course, I do
feel as though he's been influenced by fiction.

He wants his real family to recognize
his forest family, and he feels as though
becoming a gentleman will aid in that goal.
However, it is hard to imagine how
being a gentleman would help with that.

I told him that being the Ultimate
Entomologist would help bring his families
together, but he told me he still wants to
be a gentleman. Not for his family, but
for himself.

The supreme leader of an evil organization
with 10,000 members. He claims he can
change the world with a single phone call.
He offers information without being asked,
then threatens to kill you because you
know too much.

I was roped into playing a game with my
life on the line. Today's game was a card
game. Luckily, it was a draw. He says that
there are three more games to play.
Is Kokichi serious about this?

He invited me to a tea party, so I assumed
the game was called off. I thought that we
were just going to have a nice time
together, but he laughed at me and
said my life was still at risk.

I played 100 games of Rock-Paper-Scissors
with Kokichi, but each one was a draw! How
is he doing this? Is this really going to end
this like he said he would?

He doesn't want my life, he wants my heart?
Is he lying again? Despite being jerked
around by his antics, I have at least
come to know him better.

Anthropology is the study of humans
expressing their humanity. Folktales only
exist where there are folk. Kiyo has a way of
explaining things that makes it easy
to understand.

He has different bathing, sleeping, and
even an exercising masks. When I expressed
my surprise at this, he told me he would
open my mind with anthropology.

Kiyo's interest in anthropology came at the
urging of his sister, who is apparently fighting
some illness. They seem very close.
She even created his uniform for him.

He knows a lot about mythology, and his
favorite story is the tale of Medusa. He told
me that the moral of that story is that humanity
can conquer nature, but not death. The way
he smiled as he said it was creepy.

He says he's encountered "the beauty
of humanity" while doing fieldwork all over
Japan. He said that he wanted to show me,
and I promised to join him on his travels.

He's equipped with many functions you
would expect the Ultimate Robot to have,
but some of them are certainly strange.
Keebo is proud of his compact, lightweight
design, but I don't quite understand.

Keebo shared the story of his miraculous
birth by Professor Idabashi, one that
transcends science. After hearing that story,
I realized he truly is the Ultimate Robot.

He came to me for advice about starting
a robot business that played to his unique
strengths. His first idea was to be a pop star,
but his singing voice is absolutely awful.

We live in an aging society, so perhaps a
caregiver business is perfect for him. We
tried to do some caretaking practice, but as
he lifted me up, he hurt his back immediately.
Perhaps that business is not for him.

Keebo wants to experience the same
emotions we all do, and he wants to be
friends with us all. I vowed to help him with
whatever career he chose, not as a
human to a robot, but a friend to a friend.

A genuine maid who takes every word
as an order. She makes wonderful tea
and her abilities are endless.

She told me that she has helped many people
rise to greatness, and that she senses
greatness in me. She claims that if she
becomes my maid, I can walk the same
path to glory that her previous masters did.

Maids must train many skills, even combat.
Kirumi says that she has even taken down
a crime syndicate to protect her master.

She seems perfect, but she has experienced
failure. She once coddled one of her masters
too much, until he became totally dependent
on her. She has since vowed to never
make that mistake again.

She says that she sees even more potential
in me. She wants to serve me as a maid,
completely free of charge. I promised her
that I would consider her offer after we escape.

She seems like a lazy girl, but she's constantly
performing complicated magic tricks. Curious
about this apparent discrepancy, I talked to
her about it, and discovered that she trained
under a great mage to be the Ultimate Magician.

Her master is a legendary mage known
around the world. She likes to talk at length
about her days training under him, but when
I asked where he was now, she went silent.

She told me about why she parted ways
with her master. While on a traveling magic
show with her master, her own magical talent
began to surpass his. She began to earn
more praise than he did.

Himiko ended up saving her master during
a magic trick gone awry, and he ran away
from the shame. She has not seen him since.

She believes her master is secretly training to
catch up to her one day, and that is why
she insists on developing her own magic
ability. I promised to help her reconcile
with her master when we got out.

Maki belongs to a cult-like society
of assassins. If anything happens to
her, she will never be able to return.

Kill the target you've been told to kill.
It doesn't matter if it's your friend from
school, or someone completely innocent.
She explained it to me, saying that she is
a killer, but she could be killed as well.

The orphanage she grew up in was a
facility for training future assassins. She
was scouted and endured hellish training.
She claims she's doing this for someone,
but will give no details.

I discovered that Maki was talking about
her best friend from the orphanage. She
volunteered to be an assassin to take the
place of her friend. She said all this as
if it was totally ordinary.

Her best friend died. But she says that she'll
continue to be an assassin to protect the
orphanage, the place filled with memories.
I tried to offer a way to help her, but she
refused. But still, I feel closer to her.

I tried to uncover the origin of Tenko's
intense hatred of men, but all she offered
was ways in which she hates them. I also
tend to get thrown a lot when speaking to
her. This is pretty serious.

Tenko told me the story of how she was sent
to a temple to train as a child, to rid her of
her excess energy. The chief priest became
her master, and they developed Neo-Aikido
together. It was quite confusing.

She claims to be the hero of justice, the
embodiment of the philosophy of Neo-Aikido:
world peace. She is working hard to
accomplish her goal, but her methods are
brutal, and she's extra tough on boys.

In the middle of one of her speeches about
how being touched by a man makes her
Neo-Aikido weaker, I pointed out that
her master was also a man. She hasn't
been the same since.

She finally arrived at the conclusion that
even degenerate males can improve
ourselves through Neo-Aikido. She even
said that she respected me as an equal
in our goal of mastering Neo-Aikido.

She enjoys passionately explaining to
me why she is so plain. She gets skipped
during roll call, she can walk into movie
theaters undetected, and her underwear
is plain white. At least she's having a good time.

Tsumugi opened up to me about things that
worry her about cosplaying. But despite
her doubts, she never forgets the joy of
cosplaying. Perhaps that is what makes
her the Ultimate Cosplayer.

She told me even more stories about the
fun she's had while cosplaying. She explained
makeup, crossplay, photoshoots with
friends, even accidents that have happened
during events. She's enjoying it to the fullest.

Tsumugi told me that the reason she became
so obsessed with cosplay is because a
famous cosplayer praised her first costume.
She claims to still be close friends with them.

She discovered that we both like the same
hero and told me that she would make his
costume for me to wear at an event.
Inspired by her passion, I agreed to do it.

Her birthplace is a divine island paradise
where Atua dwells, somewhere far out
at sea. The island is remote, but apparently
it's a shipping hub, and so Angie's people
have been living pretty well.

Angie's island has many customs. If you
are lonely at night, you stab a sickle into
your window. Intense physical workouts
for entering adulthood. Wedding dances
last until the sun comes up. How strange.

Most people faint when they first see
Angie's art, but those who don't are
"chosen." I fainted, and she claimed that
I was missing something that she could
give me through lust, but I declined.

Angie is cherished on her island as
an oracle of Atua. No one goes against
her word, as it is the word of Atua.
But I'm still not convinced that she isn't
mistaking her own will for Atua's will.

Angie finally seemed to separate her own
desires from Atua's for once. She wanted
to reward me for helping her come to this
epiphany by being my bride. I'm not sure I
can do that, but I am glad to be closer to her.

The inventions Miu shows off are all
incredible, but so absurd that they seem
like a waste of technology. She seems to
have taken a liking to me after I 
supported her eccentric inventing habit.

She gifted me some of her inventions,
but I wasn't sure how to react to them.
She seemed to be happy that I was
grateful for them, though, and told me
a secret she hasn't shared with anyone.

Ever since her car accident left her teetering
between life and death, she's been getting
a steady stream of ideas for inventions.
She claims this is evidence that she is a
cyborg, and I barely managed to calm her down.

Miu's moods are fickle and wild. She took
her clothes off and tried to get me to take
mine off, too. She's behaving stranger than
usual lately. When I told her I was worried
about her, she said she loved me.

She expresses her love in strange ways.
I honestly don't know how to handle it.
She even gave me her panties and
told me that she wants to go on a
date with me when we get out.

The Ultimate Pianist, so talented that
VIPs from across the world come to
watch her perform. But she laughs all
of that off, saying that she'll always be
known as the "piano freak."

She asked me to play a duet with her after
I expressed interest in the piano. When we
were playing, I felt our bodies touch, but
she was so absorbed in the music she didn't
notice. She truly is a piano freak.

Kaede says that the reason she plays the
piano is because she loves seeing people
smile. Because music reaches people's
hearts. And in order to see even more smiles,
she wants to break the boundaries of music.

Today, Kaede asked me all about my
interests, like my hobbies and my
favorite food. It seemed as though she
was taking notes, but she wouldn't
tell me what for.

We've practiced the duet quite a bit, and it's
starting to sound pretty decent. She blushed
at me when she said she wanted to invite
me over to play at her house someday.
I said that I would love that.

People call him the Ultimate Detective,
but most of his jobs are pretty simple!
For runaways, though, he said that his
job was to find out the reason they ran
away and resolve it. Being sympathetic
like that is how he and his uncle work.

His first job was to find a classmate's pet.
He worked very hard for little reward, but
I told him that the world needs more
detectives like him. That got him to blush.

Kaito asked me to teach him how to
play the piano for when he meets aliens.
He wants to communicate with them 
through music. It sounds silly, but 
music does have power 
that words don't...

He says that it's not just about going to
space—it's about finding a new path for
humanity to follow him. He wants to bring
art and technology into space with him.
He's not always logical, but there's 
an intense power to his words.

He likes animals, especially cats. He once
had one as a pet. I just know that his tired
heart will feel at ease once he gets to see
his cat again. He said that he gave it to
someone when he became a prisoner.

Ryoma tried to convince me not to get
involved with him, but I told him to stop
being so stubborn about who he is inside.
I think my words may have gotten through
to him, just a little bit.

He's very aware of his surroundings and
able to make good observations and 
rational decisions. It's almost like he's
used to doing this kind of thing...

I told him that I wanted to be friends 
after we got out, and that seemed to
encourage him a little. He said that
he would work hard to make that 
happen. He sort of sounded like
a cornered animal.

He still hasn't completely lost the habits
he picked up from living in the forest, 
so his understanding of being a 
"gentleman" is a little bit off. He still
has a lot to learn.

Gonta was frustrated by not being able to
be a proper escort for a lady, but I convinced
him that there were plenty of things about
him that made him a gentleman. That
seemed to help his confidence.

He lies and misbehaves because he says
we met before and I didn't remember him?
I racked my brain, but I don't remember
him at all. He could just be lying.

He wants me, the Ultimate Pianist, to team
up with him, the Ultimate Supreme Leader.
I rejected him immediately, but I wonder
what exactly he was planning.

Kiyo told me that music is an important
part of folklore and anthropology. He 
said that a lot of lullabies have lost
their true meaning over the years.

Kiyo was impressed by how hard I was
working to escape and told me that he
thinks his sister and I should be friends.
She's been in and out of hospitals since
she was a kid. He said he'd have to come
up with a good plan for having us meet.

I was totally blown away by Keebo, a
real live robot! I asked him a ton of 
questions, and he didn't seem to mind.
He actually seemed to like it and 
thought it was kind of fun.

I found out about Keebo's emergency
button and told him that he should
hide it better, as soon as possible!

Kirumi is researching all of us to try
to make our stay here more comfortable.
I think she must have been the mothering
type before she was the Ultimate Maid.

I told her that a true servant sees their
master as a person, and acts in order
to help their needs. She seemed to
take that to heart.

I tried to motivate the poor girl, but she
absolutely refuses to put any effort
into anything. How did she live like this?

Himiko said that her magic puts smiles
on people's faces, in a special way.
I really understand where she's coming
from. I think we bonded a little about that.

Her title is the Ultimate Child Caregiver,
but she has no idea why kids like her.
When I told her it was because she
truly loves kids deep down, she
left in a huff.

I suggested playing the piano at
her orphanage for the children.
She told me not to get involved.

Tenko is worried about Shuichi getting
too close to me. But I'm really just
baffled that her hatred of men
runs that deep!

Tenko says that she looks up to 
performers. That's partly why she's
so attached to Himiko. I told her 
that maybe, after we escape, 
she can work on becoming some
kind of Neo-Aikido performer or
something.

Communication is key for cosplayers.
We might not understand each other,
but she seems to get very excited
about typical otaku topics. We might
be able to get along!

Tsumugi and I bonded over our
passion for our hobbies. It's 
something we have in common,
even though we're worlds apart.

Angie seems to be really interested
in the piano as an art form. Of course,
when I told her that I don't believe in
Atua, she tried to convert me.

She suggested a collaborative art piece,
where I play the piano and she paints. 
I really liked that idea, but I don't
want to obey Atua or anything.

I really try my best with this girl, but
sometimes the things she says just
go too far. When I snap and argue
with her, she seems to enjoy it,
oddly enough...

Miu told me that the reason she was
happy when I was arguing with her was
because she's never had a friend to argue
with before. She thanked me for helping
her understand "plebs" or something.
